title: mmt port --jar ports Fabric mods too
text: The scoreboard reads Fabric jars in Mojang's names (step 44); the port must hand them back in the names Fabric runs: intermediary of the target release before 26.1, Mojang's from 26.1, with refmaps and access wideners written for it. Then exposure.py load starts ported Fabric mods on a real Fabric server, as it does for NeoForge.
finish: exposure.py load --loader fabric --from 1.21.1 --to 1.21.2 starts the standalone Fabric mods that link on a real 1.21.2 Fabric server and every one that links loads
wrongIf: a Fabric mod that links fails to load for a name the reading got wrong
result: mmt port --jar takes Fabric jars: read in Mojang's names (ModNames), ported, and handed back in the target release's intermediary with overrides, calls, mixin strings, accessors, the access widener, refmaps and nested jars written for it. On a real Fabric server with Fabric API, every standalone mod that links and runs on a server loads: 8 of 8 on 1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 (8 more are client-only), 10 of 10 on 1.20.6 -> 1.21 (11 client-only), mixin-heavy ones included (ferrite-core, packet-fixer). Scoreboard: 42 of 150 Fabric mods link on 1.21.2 (40 before). Client-only mods need a client start (step 51); 26.1 and later run Mojang's names and are handed back as ported.
